item.title: Overgrown tree completely obstructing view, 27th October
item.description:
At the pinned location (on the end of Suez Road), the trees and bushes/ hedges are so overgrown that the main road Mollison Avenue is completely out of view. When moving off from here you are left guessing if someone is coming at almost 40mph. The trees block a speed sign, lorries are always parked here overnight and exit from here all the time. It is extremely dangerous and has been an issue for years. Please just trim the trees/ bushes to make the oncoming traffic actually visible, this will save lives and remind people it is 30mph not 40mph as it is just beforehand.
Nearest address to the pin placed on the map (from OS Places API): Suez Road, Enfield

item.title: Outside 1 Loveridge Mews, 27th October
item.description:
I am writing to report a damaged cast-iron bollard and deteriorating pavement outside the entrance to our clinic Chatsworth centre The bollard, which is intended to protect the entrance area from vehicles, has been knocked out of position, and its decorative top cap is missing. Additionally, the surrounding pavement and asphalt are damaged and uneven, creating a potential trip hazard for pedestrians and visitors to our clinic. We are particularly concerned about the safety of our clients, including elderly visitors and those with limited mobility. We kindly request that Camden Council arrange an inspection of the area and take the necessary steps to: Repair or replace the damaged bollard, including its missing top cap. Repair the damaged asphalt and restore the pavement to a safe condition. Ensure that the bollard continues to provide protection against vehicles. We have attached photographs clearly showing the damage. We would appreciate your prompt attention to these issues and confirmation of when an inspection or repair can be arranged.

Nearest road to the pin placed on the map (automatically generated by OpenStreetMap): Loveridge Mews, Kilburn, Greater London

item.title: Household rubbish scattered across pavement outside 39 Ross Way, 27th October
item.description:
A substantial quantity of household rubbish has been left scattered across the public pavement outside 39 Ross Way, SE9 6RJ, beside the residential wheelie bins. The rubbish includes discarded food packaging, plastic bags and other household waste. It is obstructing part of the pedestrian walkway and creating an unhygienic environment, potentially attracting vermin. I discovered the rubbish on the evening of 27 October 2026. I do not know who is responsible or whether the waste was deliberately dumped or scattered from refuse bags. Please arrange for the entire affected section of pavement to be thoroughly cleaned as soon as possible and investigate the circumstances of the incident. Two photographs showing the condition of the pavement are attached.

Nearest address to the pin placed on the map (from OS Places API): Ross Way, Eltham
Report on FixMyStreet
